calls.head: The Canadiens should drive the play
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Canadiens have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Jets near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Canadiens’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

calls.head: The Canadiens hunt better looks than the Jets
calls.body: The Canadiens wait for good looks, but the Jets settle for hopeful ones. Montréal is one of the league’s best for shot quality, and Winnipeg is one of the worst. The more dangerous chances should be the Canadiens’.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Connor ties it with 33 seconds left, and the Jets win it in overtime
paras: What a comeback. The Jets won for the first time in ten games, after going 0-7-2. Tyrel Bauer had a Gordie Howe hat trick: a goal, an assist and a fight. Owen Beck opened the scoring for the Canadiens early in the first, and Josh Anderson made it 2-0 late in the period. Cole Caufield stretched the lead to 3-0 on the power play early in the second. There were five goals in the third period alone. Caufield scored again on the power play just 46 seconds into the period to make it 4-0. Arber Xhekaj and Bauer dropped the gloves midway through the period, and Florian Xhekaj and Adam Lowry squared off late in the period. Bauer, in his tenth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Cole Koepke, with less than three minutes left to get the Jets on the board. Morgan Barron cut Montréal’s lead to 4-2 with just under two minutes left. With the goalie pulled and a minute left, Kyle Connor pulled the Jets within one, and he struck again on the power play with 33 seconds left to tie it 4-4. Dylan Samberg won it in overtime, with Lowry picking up his 300th NHL point on the goal.

The Jets had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Canadiens 47-22. Stuart Skinner made 18 saves for the Jets, and Jacob Fowler stopped 42 of 47 at the other end. The loss ended Fowler’s seven-game winning streak. The Jets moved to 5-8-3, seventh in the Central, while the Habs dropped to 9-3-3, second in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Canadiens’ five-game heater is over.
The Canadiens scored on the power play for the first time since Oct 17, after going 0-for-15 over six games.
Gabriel Vilardi extended his point streak against Montréal to seven games.
Owen Beck scored his first goal of the season, his first since Dec 20, 2025 (eleven games played since).
